name: ch9_oltc_led
title: OLTC-led distribution voltage control: taps act at half the deviation, DER stay on interface Q
description: Derived from ch9_alt_lowwear (candidate 399e30d3b60b), 2026-09-11.
Two changes, both from the Stage-I analytic rules, nothing hand-guessed:
1. g_w_dso_oltc set by the commit rule for a 0.010 pu engagement
deviation instead of 0.020, so the subordinate taps act at roughly
half the voltage error they previously needed (15.72 -> 6.26).
2. g_q and g_w_dso_der scaled TOGETHER by 2. DER response to interface-Q
error goes as g_q/g_w_dso_der and is therefore unchanged, while their
response to voltage error goes as dso_g_v/g_w_dso_der and halves.
The DER Q-to-voltage attention ratio doubles, 25.3 -> 50.7, at no cost
in Q tracking speed.
NOT yet validated in closed loop: the OLTC loop gain dso_g_v/g_w_dso_oltc
rises 567 -> 1423, and lowering a tap price is the direction that produces
hunting. Run the evented bank before trusting it.
shunt_int_g_w added 2026-09-11. It sits in the gauge-invariance group with
the nine weights, so it must travel with the parameter set; leaving it in
make_config at its old-gauge value of 10 made the eight shunt banks inert
for the entire campaign (accumulated state peaked at 0.395 Mvar against a
22.5 Mvar commit threshold, zero commits in 5 h with disturbances).
Value 0.03 derived from a 30 min persistence at the measured p90 boundary
pressure |g_H| = 0.133; the independent gauge-consistent rescale of the old
value gives 0.040, so the two routes agree within 30 %.
A single very large demand may still commit within one supervisory period:
the anti-windup clamp (25 Mvar) sits above the threshold (22.5), and that
behaviour was accepted as desirable rather than designed out.
